Check Monte Carlo Precision of Scale Probabilities

Source: R/bayes_scale_probabilities.R
diagnose_bayes_probabilities.Rd

Estimate the posterior probability that each fitted kernel scale lies at or below thresholds you name, and report how precisely the original sampling chains pin down each probability.

Usage

diagnose_bayes_probabilities(
  object,
  thresholds,
  scale = c("distance", "log"),
  mcse_target = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted multiScale_bayes() object that keeps its original, unpermuted post-warmup chains from NUTS (sampler) or slice sampling (chains). Compact, thinned, and approximate fits return an unavailable report, because permuted draws cannot recover chain order.

thresholds

A nonempty named list of numeric vectors. Each name selects a fitted landscape predictor, and each vector holds distinct finite scale thresholds. Every threshold is applied to every distinct fitted combination of scale covariates and groups for that predictor. For example, list(habitat = c(100, 250)) checks two scales in projected map units.

scale

"distance" (default) means thresholds are positive kernel scales in map units. "log" means they are natural logs of those scales. Thresholds refer to the scale parameters summarized by posterior_scales(), not to transformed kernel-weight radii such as those from kernel_dist().

mcse_target

Optional target for the Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE) on the probability axis, strictly between 0 and 1. For example, 0.005 asks for an MCSE no larger than half a percentage point. The default NULL reports precision without judging it against a target.

Value

A list with these elements.

  • available, reason: whether the original chains could be read, and an explanation when they could not. A single event can lack precision estimates even when the report is available.

  • raw_diagnostics: the fit's original diagnostics, unchanged.

  • probabilities: a data frame with one row per fitted scale combination and threshold. covariate, group, row, threshold, and threshold_scale identify the event. estimate is the posterior probability that the scale is at or below the threshold. mcse, ess_mean, and rhat are the Monte Carlo standard error, mean effective sample size, and rank-normalized Rhat of the event indicator. constant flags an indicator that never changed. precision_available is TRUE when the MCSE and mean ESS are finite and positive. precision_target_met compares mcse with mcse_target, and is NA when no target was given. reason explains missing precision. rhat_available and rhat_reason report separately whether Rhat could be computed. Undefined values are NA.

  • chain_probabilities: the same event identifiers with chain, that chain's estimate, and whether its indicator is constant. Large differences among chains signal poor mixing.

  • chains, iterations: the number of chains and of post-warmup iterations per chain, or NA when unavailable.

  • mcse_target, event, notes: the requested target, the event definition ("kernel_scale <= threshold"), and the limits of interpretation.

  • metadata_establishes_eligibility: always FALSE. The report does not change the fit's sampling or derived-scale diagnostic gates.

Read the precision

The MCSE is computational uncertainty in the probability estimate, not posterior uncertainty about the scale and not observation variation. precision_target_met only compares that MCSE with your target. It does not override Rhat, ESS, the raw sampler checks, or model checks, and a small MCSE cannot rule out an unvisited tail or mode. Read diagnose_bayes_scales() alongside this report, and compare independent runs when a consequential probability remains uncertain. Longer chains reduce the MCSE.

How the events are computed

Each event is evaluated on fitted log scales in map units, which avoids overflow from exponentiating distances. The posterior package computes the mean ESS, MCSE, and rank-normalized Rhat of each binary indicator. At least two chains with four retained iterations each are needed for precision diagnostics. A constant indicator has no estimable precision, even when its probability is exactly zero or one. Indicator Rhat can be undefined for a balanced binary event even when the MCSE is finite. It is then reported as NA with its own flag and reason, which alone does not make the precision unavailable. A nonfinite derived log scale is an error, and iterations are never dropped.

The function does not fit a model, change priors, simulate new groups, or treat importance candidates as MCMC chains. Reading a full NUTS sampler can take substantial memory, but the report keeps only summaries. vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") shows how to report a probability with its MCSE.

See also

diagnose_bayes_scales(), posterior_scales(), predict_scales(), diagnose_bayes_laplace(), multiScaleR_bayes

Examples

# A stored slice fit that keeps its four original chains
shared <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-bayesian-scales.rds",
  package = "multiScaleR"))$fit
if (requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  report <- diagnose_bayes_probabilities(shared,
    thresholds = list(land1 = c(200, 300)), mcse_target = 0.01)
  # Probability that sigma for land1 is at most 200 m and at most 300 m
  print(report$probabilities[c("threshold", "estimate", "mcse",
                               "precision_target_met")])
  print(report$chain_probabilities[c("threshold", "chain", "estimate")])
}
#>   threshold estimate        mcse precision_target_met
#> 1       200  0.08175 0.007034019                 TRUE
#> 2       300  0.90425 0.008701902                 TRUE
#>   threshold chain estimate
#> 1       200     1    0.059
#> 2       200     2    0.078
#> 3       200     3    0.089
#> 4       200     4    0.101
#> 5       300     1    0.898
#> 6       300     2    0.903
#> 7       300     3    0.893
#> 8       300     4    0.923

# A compact fit keeps thinned, permuted draws and cannot be checked
example <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bayesian-annual-example.rds",
  package = "multiScaleR"))
compact <- diagnose_bayes_probabilities(example$fits$pooled,
  thresholds = list(habitat = c(100, 250)))
compact$available   # FALSE
#> [1] FALSE
compact$reason
#> [1] "Full unpermuted MCMC chains are not retained; stored permuted or thinned draws cannot recover them."
